node.name: capture
node.description: transparent alias for the external `capture` CLI
node.whenToUse: you need to drive a real browser — screenshot, measure rendered geometry, capture a HAR or accessibility tree, or run JS against a live page. The browser is one crtr launches itself, carrying none of the user's logins: use `crtr device` instead when the page needs their session or the task is to act inside a web app on their behalf.

passthrough.installHint: Install the Capture CLI: npm install -g @crouton-kit/capture

rootEntry.concept: browser automation for agents via the external Capture CLI (CDP screenshots, HAR, a11y, JS-exec, and site libs)
rootEntry.description: forwards verbatim to the external `capture` binary
rootEntry.whenToUse: a claim depends on what a real browser renders. When it depends on rendered geometry, clipping, overflow, stacking or nominal box intersection, computed style, or distance, read `crtr capture measure -h` — screenshots and accessibility trees orient but do not establish rendered structure. This drives a browser crtr launches itself and holds none of the user's sessions — to act inside the user's own logged-in browser use `crtr device`, and to read a public page for its content rather than its rendering use `crtr search`.

node.summary: transparent alias for the external `capture` CLI — every argument forwards verbatim
node.model: This branch owns no schema of its own: it execs `capture` with whatever args follow, inherits stdio, and propagates its exit code. Run `crtr capture -h` for capture's real command tree. Every browser it drives is a fresh one crtr launched, so anything requiring the user's login belongs on `crtr device` instead.
